newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Witnesses say Zaire president's village not looted.
newsitem.headline: Witnesses say Zaire president's village not looted.

text.p: Independent sources on Friday confirmed official Zairean denials that President Mobutu Sese Seko's home village was looted by his own troops this week.
A regional military source, quoted by Reuters from rebel-held Lubumbashi on Wednesday, said retreating troops looted Gbadolite, where Mobutu has two residences.
Zaire Information Minister Kin-Kiey Mulumba denied the report on Thursday at a news conference and presidential sources also told Reuters it was false.
Independent corroboration of the denial came on Friday from two foreign journalists, Frederic Fritscher of the French daily Le Monde and photographer Robert Grossman, working for the New York Times.
They were flown on Thursday aboard a Zairean military aircraft to Gbadolite, near the border with Central Afrcan Republic. They found it peaceful and under government control.
"We visited the president's two residences, which are 10 km (six miles) apart, Gbadolite village and the market and there was absolutely no sign of looting," Fritscher told Reuters in Kinshasa.
"The situation looked quite normal," he said.

In the course of the seven-month rebellion, spokesmen for Laurent Kabila's rebels have on several occasions prematurely reported the fall of government-held towns or their looting by retreating troops.
Mobutu's government says this is a disinformation tactic aimed at demoralising defending forces and local people.
